summary: Canada is well documented: the 2014 federal evaluation gives federal investor applications, approvals, refusals, withdrawals and admissions for 2007-2011, the pending inventory (66,368 persons in Feb 2014) and capital raised by the federal and Quebec programmes; the budget, the terminating statute (s. 87.5 IRPA) and the Federal Court of Appeal record the 2014 closure; ministerial instructions and IRCC bulletins document the failed 2015 venture capital pilot; Quebec gazette orders, the 2023 regulation, a MIFI impact analysis (15.5% of 2011-2020 investor admits still in Quebec) and an Investissement Québec access response (loans by year, collapsing to C$1-3 million after the 2024 overhaul) cover Quebec, with IRCC open data giving admissions 2015-2026 by province and nationality. For Latin America the legal thresholds are documented for Costa Rica (US$200,000 to US$150,000 in 2021), Argentina (ARS 1.5 million since 2010), Brazil (business and real-estate routes, with 2023-2025 counts and values from OBMigra) and Uruguay (where investment only confers tax residence); Paraguay and Mexico could not be documented because official sites were blocked or unreachable.

programs.name: Canada federal Immigrant Investor Program (Investor class, Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations ss. 88-109)
programs.notes: Permanent residence (no conditions after arrival) for experienced business people who lent the federal government a fixed sum for five years without interest; the money was passed to participating provinces and territories and repaid. C$400,000 loan and C$800,000 net worth until 30 Nov 2010, then C$800,000 and C$1.6 million. Introduced 1986, redesigned 1 April 1999. Cap of 700 new applications a year from 1 July 2011; intake stopped 1 July 2012. Budget 2014 (11 Feb 2014) announced its end; section 87.5 IRPA (Economic Action Plan 2014 Act, No. 1, assent 19 June 2014) terminated every application not assessed before 11 Feb 2014 and ordered refunds (it did not apply to investors selected by Quebec). Ordinary naturalisation rules apply afterwards (no investor-specific route). The 2014 CIC evaluation found investor immigrants declared low incomes and paid little income tax, had the highest out-migration after 10 years, and that only about 30% of the loan money was actively invested.

programs.name: Canada Immigrant Investor Venture Capital (IIVC) pilot (Immigrant Investor Venture Capital class, ministerial instructions under IRPA s. 14.1)
programs.notes: Replacement pilot for the federal IIP: permanent residence for up to 60 investors with net worth of at least C$10 million who paid C$2 million, not guaranteed, into a venture capital fund (held about 15 years and managed mainly by BDC Capital, per CBC), plus language and education requirements and a due diligence report. Intake windows 28 Jan-11 Feb 2015 (max 500 applications), 13 Feb-15 Apr 2015 and 25 May-30 Dec 2015. IRCC told CBC only seven applications were in process when intake closed on 30 Dec 2015. IRCC declared the pilot closed and removed its instructions on 29 Jan 2021 after finalising the last files. Final admissions not found.

programs.name: Quebec Investor Program (Programme des investisseurs, Règlement sur l'immigration au Québec, art. 37 and following)
programs.notes: Quebec selects the investor (selection certificate, CSQ) under the Canada-Quebec Accord; IRCC then grants permanent residence. Investors place a fixed sum for 5 years with IQ Immigrants Investisseurs (a subsidiary of Investissement Québec) through an authorised broker or trust company; the income funds grants to Quebec businesses. Placement of C$1,200,000 (net worth C$2 million) under the regulation in force from 2 August 2018 (the amount before then was not confirmed in a Quebec text in this pass); from 1 January 2024 a C$1,000,000 placement plus a non-refundable C$200,000 contribution, oral French level 7, a work permit and stays of at least 6 months each for the investor and spouse in Quebec (no stay required before). Receipt of applications was suspended 1 Apr-15 Aug 2018; capped at 1,900 (max 1,235 from China) for 10 Sep 2018-31 Aug 2019; suspended again 1 Nov 2019 to 1 Apr 2023. Under the new rules only C$1 million (2024-25) and C$3 million (Apr-Dec 2025) of placements were made. MIFI found only 15.5% of people admitted 2011-2020 still present in Quebec in January 2022. Launch year of the Quebec programme is not stated in the sources read (the federal investor class dates from 1986).

programs.name: Brazil residence authorisation for investors (autorização de residência para investidor: Resolução Normativa CNIg 13/2017, business; RN 36/2018 as replaced by RN 46, real estate)
programs.notes: Two routes under the 2017 Migration Law (Lei 13.445) and Decreto 9.199/2017, set by resolutions of the National Immigration Council (CNIg): investment of own foreign funds in a Brazilian company (R$150,000 under RN 84/2009; R$500,000 from RN 118/2015, kept by RN 13/2017) and purchase of urban residential property with foreign funds (RN 36/2018: R$1,000,000, R$700,000 in the North and Northeast; replaced by RN 46, which kept the amounts and per the Agência Gov release gives an initial authorisation of up to four years, renewable). Granted by the Ministry of Justice (CGIL). 252 business and 290 real-estate authorisations in 2025. Naturalisation follows general rules. Launch shown as 2009 (RN 84); earlier investor rules were not checked.

programs.name: Costa Rica temporary residence as investor (residencia temporal, categoría inversionista: Ley General de Migración y Extranjería 8764 art. 79; Reglamento de Extranjería arts. 87-93; Ley 9996)
programs.notes: Temporary residence for a foreigner who invests at least US$200,000 (Reglamento de Extranjería 2012, art. 87) in real estate, registrable goods, shares, securities, productive projects or projects of national interest; Ley 9996 (in force 14 July 2021) set a new minimum of US$150,000 "for the period set by this law", added venture capital funds and sustainable tourism projects, and gave tax and import exemptions that could be claimed only in the first five years (to July 2026). Whether the US$150,000 threshold continues after July 2026 is unclear from the law's wording; not resolved in this pass. Run by the Dirección General de Migración y Extranjería (DGME). No official counts found. Launch date of the investor category before the 2012 regulation not checked.

programs.name: Argentina temporary residence as investor (residencia temporaria, subcategoría inversionista: Ley de Migraciones 25.871 art. 23; Decreto 616/2010, Anexo art. 23 d)
programs.notes: Temporary residence for a foreigner making a productive, commercial or service investment of interest to the country of at least ARS 1,500,000 (fixed in pesos in the 2010 decree), with proof of the lawful origin of the funds and their entry through banks authorised by the central bank, and a non-binding opinion of the industry ministry on the project. Distinct from the 2025 citizenship-by-investment route (arg-cbi). Launch shown as the date of the regulatory decree; the subcategory exists in the 2004 law. No official counts found; later changes to the amount not found in this pass.

programs.name: Uruguay tax residence through investment (residencia fiscal por inversión, Decreto 148/007 art. 5-BIS, as amended)
programs.notes: Not an immigration permit: Uruguay's migration law (Ley 18.250) has no investor category. An individual is treated as a Uruguayan TAX resident if they hold an investment of more than 15,000,000 UI in real estate or more than 45,000,000 UI in a business with projects of national interest (criteria added by Decreto 330/016 of 13 Oct 2016), or, for investments from 1 July 2020, more than 3,500,000 UI in real estate plus at least 60 days' presence a year, or more than 15,000,000 UI in a business creating 15 jobs (Decretos 163/020 and 174/020). UI (Unidad Indexada) is an inflation-indexed unit. Further investment-linked tax options (impatriate regimes) were added in 2021 and 2026. Launch shown as the date the investment criteria were added.

gaps: Canada federal IIP: no official count of applications and persons terminated by s. 87.5 in June 2014 (only the evaluation's inventory of 66,368 persons on 4 Feb 2014), and no yearly federal admissions series before 2007 or split from Quebec in 2012-2014 (IRCC Facts & Figures combine federal and Quebec investors).
Canada federal IIP: no data on the total refunded or on repayments of the provincial loans.
IIVC pilot: final number of applications approved and investors admitted not found (IRCC shows no separate category in open data; only CBC's report of seven applications in process at 30 Dec 2015).

Quebec Investor Program: no MIFI yearly series of selection certificates (CSQ) issued to investors, or by nationality, was found; admissions by nationality exist only for the combined Investor category (IRCC). Admissions by year before 2015 split from federal investors not found, except investment capital 2007-2011 in the federal evaluation.

Quebec: thresholds before August 2018 (C$800,000 placement / C$1.6 million net worth from late 2010, C$400,000 / C$800,000 before) were not confirmed in a Quebec regulatory text; the final 2018 RIQ (décret 963-2018) was not downloaded (only the draft). LégisQuébec blocked downloads (HTTP 403).

Quebec: no audit by the Vérificateur général du Québec or other official evaluation of the investor programme was found; the reopening date for applications under the 2024 rules and any intake caps after April 2023 were not found.

Brazil: yearly counts of investor authorisations before 2023 and for 2024 were not collected (OBMigra annual and CGIL quarterly reports for 2015-2024 exist but were not read); the texts of RN 84/2009, RN 118/2015, RN 13/2017, RN 36/2018 and RN 46 were not downloaded (Diário Oficial search failed), so dates and amounts come from the OBMigra report and a government news release.

Costa Rica: no official count of investor residences granted (DGME site returned HTTP 403); status of the US$150,000 threshold after July 2026 unresolved; Ley 8764 art. 79 not read; the regulation of Ley 9996 (Decreto 43926-MGP-H-TUR, 2023) not read.
Argentina: no DNM statistics on investor residences found; whether the ARS 1,500,000 amount was ever updated not confirmed.
Uruguay: no immigration residence-by-investment route exists in Ley 18.250 as read; no counts of people using the tax-residence-by-investment criteria found.

Paraguay: nothing documented. The migration agency (migraciones.gov.py) returned HTTP 403 and the congressional library (bacn.gov.py) search did not return Ley 6984/2022; investor residence rules and any counts remain unread.
